title: 孟德尔的豌豆：遗传学如何开始
topic: How Mendel's pea experiments founded the science of genetics

sentences.en: Today I want to talk about heredity, the simple fact that offspring resemble their parents, and how one monk with a garden of peas turned that everyday observation into the science we now call genetics.
sentences.zh: 今天我想聊聊遗传，也就是后代长得像父母这个简单事实，以及一位修士如何用一园子豌豆，把这个日常观察变成了我们如今所说的遗传学。

sentences.en: Before Gregor Mendel, most people assumed that a hereditary trait from each parent simply blended in the child, like mixing two colors of paint.
sentences.zh: 在孟德尔之前，大多数人以为父母双方各自的遗传性状会在孩子身上简单混合，就像把两种颜色的颜料调在一起。

sentences.en: Mendel doubted that, so in the 1860s he began to cross pea plants and count exactly what each generation of offspring looked like.
sentences.zh: 孟德尔对此心存怀疑，于是在十九世纪六十年代，他开始给豌豆植株杂交，并精确统计每一代后代长什么样。

sentences.en: He chose traits that were easy to see, such as whether a plant produced round seeds or wrinkled ones, purple flowers or white.
sentences.zh: 他挑选了那些一眼就能看出的性状，比如植株结的种子是圆的还是皱的，开的花是紫色还是白色。

sentences.en: When he crossed a purple-flowered plant with a white one, the hybrid offspring were not a blended pale purple; every single one was fully purple.
sentences.zh: 当他把开紫花的植株和开白花的植株杂交时，得到的杂交后代并不是混合出来的淡紫色，而是每一株都是纯正的紫色。

sentences.en: The white trait had not disappeared, though, because when those hybrids reproduced, white flowers came back in about one out of every four plants.
sentences.zh: 不过白花这个性状并没有消失，因为当这些杂交种再繁殖时，白花又在大约每四株里出现一株。

sentences.en: To explain this, Mendel proposed that each trait is controlled by a pair of hidden factors, what we today call two copies of a gene.
sentences.zh: 为了解释这一点，孟德尔提出：每个性状都由一对隐藏的因子控制，也就是我们今天所说的一个基因的两份拷贝。

sentences.en: The two versions of that gene are called alleles, and an organism inherits one allele from each parent.
sentences.zh: 这个基因的两个版本被称为等位基因，生物体从父母双方各遗传得到一个等位基因。

sentences.en: One allele can be dominant, meaning a single copy is enough to show up, while the other is recessive and appears only when both copies are the recessive form.
sentences.zh: 一个等位基因可以是显性的，意思是只要有一份就能表现出来；另一个则是隐性的，只有当两份拷贝都是隐性形式时才会显现。

sentences.en: That is why the full set of genes an organism carries, its genotype, is not always the same as its visible phenotype.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么一个生物体所携带的全套基因，即它的基因型，并不总是等同于它可见的表现型。

sentences.en: A purple plant might carry one hidden recessive allele, so it looks purple yet can still transmit the white trait to its own descendants.
sentences.zh: 一株紫花植物也许携带着一个隐藏的隐性等位基因，所以它看上去是紫色的，却仍能把白花性状传给自己的后代。

sentences.en: Mendel did not know it, but those alleles sit on structures inside the cell called chromosomes, long strands of DNA wound tightly together.
sentences.zh: 孟德尔当时并不知道，那些等位基因位于细胞内一种叫染色体的结构上，也就是紧紧缠绕在一起的长长的 DNA 链。

sentences.en: DNA is a molecule shaped like a twisted ladder, and before a cell divides, it must replicate, so that each new cell receives a complete copy of the genome.
sentences.zh: DNA 是一种形状像扭转梯子的分子，在细胞分裂之前，它必须复制，好让每个新细胞都得到基因组的一份完整拷贝。

sentences.en: The exact order, or sequence, of chemical letters along that strand is what spells out the instructions inherited from an ancestor.
sentences.zh: 沿着那条链排列的化学字母的精确顺序，也就是序列，正是从祖先那里遗传下来的那套指令。

sentences.en: Sometimes a small copying error, a mutation, changes one letter, and this is the ultimate source of the genetic variation on which evolution depends.
sentences.zh: 有时一个微小的复制错误，也就是突变，会改变其中一个字母，而这正是进化所依赖的遗传变异的最终来源。

sentences.en: Not all reproduction shuffles these genes: a plant grown from a cutting is a clone, genetically identical to its single parent.
sentences.zh: 并非所有的繁殖都会重新洗牌这些基因：一株由插条长成的植物是克隆体，与它唯一的亲本在基因上完全相同。

sentences.en: So remember that Mendel counted peas and saw the rules of inheritance decades before anyone had seen a gene, and that quiet garden work is why heredity is now something we can read, letter by letter.
sentences.zh: 所以请记住，早在任何人见到基因的几十年前，孟德尔就靠数豌豆看清了遗传的规律，而正是那份安静的园艺工作，让遗传如今成了我们可以一个字母一个字母去读懂的东西。
